france24fr.title: Les négociations entre l'Iran et les États-Unis vont démarrer en Suisse
france24fr.description: Les discussions entre les États-Unis et l'Iran pour trouver une paix durable au Moyen-Orient doivent débuter dimanche matin dans un hôtel de luxe des Alpes suisses, quatre jours après la signature d'un protocole d'accord, déjà malmené, pour mettre fin aux hostilités.

france24fr.title: Présidentielle en Colombie : qui est le candidat de gauche Ivan Cepeda ?
france24fr.description: Le sénateur Ivan Cepeda, 63 ans, bénéficie de la popularité de l'allié Petro, notamment parmi les classes populaires reconnaissantes pour la réduction de la pauvreté, les salaires plus élevés et une baisse du chômage dans l'un des pays les plus inégalitaires au monde. Le philosophe et défenseur des droits de l'Homme, un temps donné favori du scrutin, a toutefois été devancé par son rival de la droite dure lors du premier tour.

france24fr.title: NTG : le parlement européen autorise les "nouveaux OGM"
france24fr.description: Un règlement sur de nouvelles techniques de modifications génétiques des plantes, dites NTG, a été adopté au Parlement européen ce mercredi. "On va permettre à des multinationales de commercialiser sur le marché européen des plantes OGM sans aucune traçabilité. Les agriculteurs ne sauront pas qu'ils sont en train de planter des OGM, et les consommateurs ne sauront pas qu'ils sont en train d'en manger", résume notre invité Jean-Mathieu Thevenot, agriculteur et membre de la Confédération Paysanne

france24fr.title: 🔴 En direct : les médiateurs pakistanais et J.D. Vance en Suisse pour des pourparlers avec l'Iran
Fête de la musique : l'alcool interdit dans les départements en vigilance rouge canicule
france24fr.description: La consommation d'alcool pour la Fête de la musique dimanche sera interdite sur la voie publique dans les 35 départements placés en vigilance rouge canicule et "consigne est donnée" de ne pas en proposer dans les évènements organisés par l'État, a annoncé samedi le gouvernement.

france24fr.title: Espagne : un tribunal interdit à l'épouse du Premier ministre de quitter le pays
france24fr.description: Un tribunal espagnol a ordonné que l'épouse du Premier ministre Pedro Sánchez, Begoña Gómez, soit jugée par un jury pour corruption et lui a interdit de quitter le pays, selon une ordonnance rendue publique samedi.

france24fr.title: La Bolivie décrète l'état d'exception, début de levée des barrages
france24fr.description: Le président bolivien Rodrigo Paz a décrété samedi 20 juin l'état d'exception dans l'ensemble de son pays après plus de six semaines de protestations et de blocages routiers, la police commençant peu après à dégager certains barrages à l'aide d'engins de chantier.

france24fr.title: Marc Bloch : un historien, un combattant, un résistant mort pour la France entre au Panthéon
france24fr.description: Quatre-vingt-deux ans après son exécution par les Allemands, l'historien et résistant Marc Bloch fait son entrée le 23 juin au Panthéon. Ce professeur spécialiste de l'histoire du Moyen Âge n'a eu de cesse tout au long de sa vie de s'engager pour la France. De la Première à la Seconde Guerre mondiale, il n'a aspiré qu'à l'action pour défendre son pays.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : pas de miracle Renard, la Tunisie prend la porte après sa déroute contre le Japon
Mondial 2026 : pas de miracle Renard, la Tunisie prend la porte après une déroute contre le Japon
france24fr.description: L'arrivée d'Hervé Renard n'a rien changé. Après l'humiliation contre la Suède, la Tunisie s'est lourdement inclinée contre le Japon dimanche (4-0) et est déjà éliminée de la Coupe du monde 2026. Les Nippons, quant à eux, entrevoient les 16es de finale.

france24fr.title: En direct : les médiateurs pakistanais et J.D. Vance en Suisse pour des pourparlers avec l'Iran
france24fr.description: Le vice-président américain J.D. Vance et les représentants pakistanais, dont le chef d'État-major Asim Munir, sont arrivés en Suisse, dimanche 21 juin, pour de nouveaux pourparlers avec l'Iran, centrés sur le programme nucléaire iranien. La délégation iranienne, composée notamment du négociateur en chef Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf et du chef de la diplomatie Abbas Araghchi, est également attendue dans la matinée. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : résultats, articles et temps forts de la nuit
france24fr.description: Les Pays-Bas en démonstration, l'Allemagne qualifiée, la Côte d'Ivoire renversée, Curaçao historique et la Tunisie humiliée par le Japon… Retrouvez les résultats des matches disputés dans la nuit, les temps forts et les derniers articles de France 24 sur la Coupe du monde 2026.

france24fr.title: Tunisie - Japon : les Aigles de Carthage sortent par la petite porte
france24fr.description: Après la déroute face à la Suède (5-1), les Aigles de Carthage jouaient leur survie dans la compétition face au Japon, dimanche à Monterrey, au Mexique. Face à des Samouraïs Bleus bien lancés par leur nul contre les Pays-Bas (2-2), les Tunisiens ont sombré. Revivez la rencontre grâce à notre direct commenté.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : l'immense exploit de Curaçao qui arrache le premier point de son histoire
france24fr.description: Curaçao a tenu le point du match nul samedi à Kansas City, dans le groupe E du Mondial 2026. Un exploit historique pour la petite île des Antilles.

france24fr.title: Colombie : la gauche au pouvoir et la droite pro-Trump dos à dos au second tour de la présidentielle
france24fr.description: Quelque 41 millions de Colombiens sont appelés à voter, dimanche, au second tour de l'élection présidentielle. Le millionnaire Abelardo de la Espriella, partisan d'une droite dure soutenu par Donald Trump, affronte le sénateur Ivan Cepeda, issu du parti du président de gauche sortant Gustavo Petro. La question des relations avec Washington les divise, comme celle de la politique à adopter face au crime organisé, entre ligne dure et tentatives de paix.

france24fr.title: Concerts annulés et alcool interdit, la canicule vient troubler la Fête de la musique
france24fr.description: Avec 41°C attendus par endroits dimanche et le nombre record de 35 départements en vigilance rouge, plusieurs départements ont pris des mesures pour éviter les accidents lors de la Fête de la musique. À Paris, en vigilance rouge, les festivités sont maintenues, mais l'alcool sera interdit sur la voie publique. Ailleurs, certains concerts sont annulés ou repoussés à plus tard dans la soirée.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : Hosni Manoubi, l'œil du football tunisien
france24fr.description: Au Mondial 2026, les Aigles de Carthage seront suivis par des millions de regards. Mais il en est un qui ne quitte jamais le terrain : celui d’Hosni Manoubi. Héritier d’une légende de la photographie sportive tunisienne, il poursuit depuis des années une histoire de famille à travers son objectif.

Kriminalität: Falsche Polizisten auf Beutezug: Seniorinnen betrogen
Brände: Brand in Dönerfabrik – Inhaber und Sohn entkommen
CDU-Landesparteitag: Bremer Regierungschefin? Winter fordert Bovenschulte heraus

zeit.title: Badeunfall: Jugendlicher beim Schwimmen im Rhein-Herne-Kanal umgekommen
Albanien: Zehntausende protestieren gegen Luxus-Bauprojekt mit Trump-Verbindung
zeit.description: Ein Bauprojekt mit Verbindungen zu Donald Trumps Familie sorgt in Albanien weiterhin für Proteste. Tausende fordern nun den Rücktritt des Regierungschefs.

zeit.title: Deutschland bei der WM: »Natürlich war es ein Glückssieg«
zeit.description: Deutschland muss gegen die Elfenbeinküste ans Limit gehen, braucht Glück und Deniz Undav. Der Videopodcast fragt sich: Ist das die berühmte deutsche Turniermannschaft?

Krieg gegen die Ukraine: Benzinverkauf auf der Krim nach ukrainischen Angriffen ausgesetzt
zeit.description: Auf der gesamten Krim wird Treibstoff nur noch an staatliche Dienste verteilt. Fähr- und Autoverkehr zwischen der Halbinsel und Russland sind unterbrochen. Das Liveblog

zeit.title: Feste: Polizei zieht positives Zwischenfazit zur Johannisnacht
Verkehr: Unfälle im Harz – mehrere Biker schwer verletzt
»Jemand, der einmal ich war«: »Was sie sagt, ist messerscharf«
zeit.description: Die Regisseurin Regina Schilling und die Schauspielerin Sandra Hüller haben einen Dokumentarfilm über Ingeborg Bachmann gedreht. Ein Gespräch

zeit.title: Ingeborg Bachmann und die Beatles: Die Beatles und die Bachmann
zeit.description: Erstmals hier zu lesen: ein Gedicht, das Ingeborg Bachmann Ende der Sechzigerjahre geschrieben hat. Es handelt von einer Band aus Liverpool.

zeit.title: Brathähnchen mit Tomatenreis: Ein Huhn, das man besingen möchte
zeit.description: Wer Tomaten, Zwiebeln und Knoblauch zusammen schmort, muss ein glücklicher Mensch sein. Hier karamellisieren ihre Säfte um Reiskörner herum, begleitet von einem Brathuhn.

observador.title: "Não escrevo para me vingar, mas há coisas de que não fujo"
observador.description: Três anos depois do best-seller "Leme", Madalena Sá Fernandes abre a porta de "Sótão", novo registo autobiográfico em torno da crueldade nas relações, dos fantasmas do passado e da solidão.

observador.title: “Começou com uma bifana”. David cozinha Portugal nos EUA
observador.description: Nasceu nos EUA, filho de portugueses, e sentiu saudade da comida de “casa”. Procurou produtos portugueses nos EUA e agora ensina os americanos a cozinhar Portugal: “Faço do bacalhau ao cozido”.

observador.title: Cabo Verde. "Já não precisam de nos procurar no Google"
observador.description: Funaná, Cachupa, tubarões e muitas mensagens em crioulo. O Esplanade Park de Fort Lauderdale vibrou com a festa de cabo-verdianos em véspera do jogo frente ao Uruguai. "Agora já estamos no mapa".

observador.title: 9h. Arranca votação para eleição dos órgãos nacionais do PSD
observador.description: Arranca a esta hora a votação para a eleição dos órgãos nacionais do PSD. Ainda, JD Vance já está na Suíça para a próxima ronda de negociações entre Estados Unidos e Irão.

observador.title: Irão e EUA voltam às negociações. JD Vance já está na Suíça
observador.description: O vice-presidente dos EUA, JD Vance, já chegou à Suíça, onde vão decorrer negociações este domingo. Governante espera "avançar na questão nuclear e na questão do cessar-fogo no Líbano".

observador.title: A incansável Katy Perry e o festão de Pedro Sampaio
observador.description: A 11.ª edição do festival arrancou dominada pela pop americana e brasileira. O parque Papa Francisco (com algumas mudanças face a 2024) esgotou e o mesmo vai acontecer este domingo, com Linkin Park.

observador.title: Espanha em busca da primeira vitória frente à Arábia Saudita
observador.description: Com México, EUA e Alemanha já qualificados para a fase seguinte, domingo arranca com Espanha à procura dos três pontos, frente à Arábia Saudita (17h00). A fechar a noite, um Uruguai-Cabo Verde.

observador.title: O que fizeram os jogadores para "blindar" Portugal?
observador.description: Uma “conversa” fora dos planos da FPF “blindou” o plantel português. Cabo Verde com funaná e cachupa em Miami. Alemanha avança. Laranja faz sueca terminar aos 5. Room, de Curaçau, é o "novo Vozinha".

observador.title: 8h. Sebastião Bugalho é vice-presidente e porta-voz do PSD
observador.description: Sebastião Bugalho, Carlos Moedas e Pedro Duarte vão passar a vice-presidentes do PSD. Ainda, devem arrancar hoje, na Suíça, as discussões técnicas para a paz entre Estados Unidos e Irão.

observador.title: Entre mundiais: o que mudou em nós em 4 anos
observador.description: Usámos o último Mundial como ponto de partida: onde estávamos em 2022, onde estamos agora. Falámos sobre o que mudou, o que deixámos para trás, e arriscámos adivinhar o próximo capítulo.

observador.title: “Nos ki ta manda”. Funaná e Cachupa na festa de Cabo Verd...
observador.description: Em Fort Lauderdale, centenas de cabo-verdianos soltaram os ritmos africanos no Esplanade Park. Nem a chuva torrencial travou a festa. "É uma coisa impensável, uma alegria enorme. Estamos no mapa."

observador.title: Rui Pêgo: "Privatizar a RTP seria um disparate monumental"
observador.description: De Luanda aos bastidores da rádio portuguesa, Rui Pêgo fala da ameaça da desinformação, da polémica em torno da privatização da RTP e da forma como o digital tem vindo a mudar a comunicação.

observador.title: A enxaqueca ainda é uma doença desvalorizada
observador.description: Quem legisla, desvaloriza a doença, alerta o neurologista Henrique Delgado. E para quem tem enxaqueca, como Isabel Pireza, os anos até chegar ao diagnóstico e tratamento são terríveis.

observador.title: 7h. Mundial 2026. Japão vence a Tunísia
observador.description: No Mundial de futebol, o Japão venceu a Tunísia por 3-0. Ainda, termina hoje o Congresso do PSD em Aveiro.

observador.title: A “conversa” em Palm Beach que “blindou” a Seleção
observador.description: Nos primeiros dias nos EUA, os jogadores da Seleção reuniram-se para “blindar” o grupo contra as críticas, principalmente das redes sociais. Todos participaram e não estava nos planos da FPF.

observador.title: O futebol viveu da magia dos samurais na sua milésima dança
observador.description: O milésimo jogo da história dos Mundiais chegou com uma goleada e uma prestação dominante do Japão, que voltou a dizimar a Tunísia, agora com Renard (0-4). Luta pelos três primeiros lugares em aberto.

observador.title: 6h. Congresso do PSD termina hoje em Aveiro
observador.description: O encerramento dos trabalhos será marcado pela eleição dos novos órgãos dirigentes e pelo discurso de encerramento de Luís Montenegro. Ainda, o Japão está a vencer a Tunísia por três bolas a zero.

observador.title: Job e Jonas: o sofrimento humano e a justiça divina
observador.description: Os livros de Job e Jonas contam as histórias de duas personagens diferentes, mas ambas funcionam como parábolas sobre a justiça e o sofrimento humano. O novo episódio de "As Histórias da Bíblia".

nzz.title: Nach dem schweren Gewitter über Zürich: 16-Jährige erliegt ihren Verletzungen
nzz.description: Ein Sommersturm hatte am Freitagabend zu Überschwemmungen und Schäden an Bäumen und Verkehrsverbindungen geführt. Eine junge Frau wurde von einem herabstürzenden Ast getroffen. Sie starb am Samstag im Spital.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Gespanntes Warten auf den Lake Lucerne Summit +++ Bericht: Sieben Tote bei neuen Angriffen Israels im Libanon
nzz.description: Zwischen den USA und Iran herrscht seit Februar 2026 Krieg, die Folgen sind weltweit spürbar. Nun scheint sich ein Ende des Konflikts anzubahnen. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Live-Ticker.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Ärger bei EU-Gipfel um Russland-Initiative Costas +++ EU verlängert Russland-Sanktionen erstmals um zwölf Monate
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten im Überblick.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Fussball-WM 2026: Tunesien scheidet gegen Japan aus +++ Deutschland wird nach einem 2:1 gegen Côte d’Ivoire Gruppensieger
nzz.description: Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten zur Fussball-WM in Kanada, Mexiko und den USA.

nzz.title: Vance in Emmen gelandet – Vizepräsident gibt sich optimistisch vor Verhandlungen in der Schweiz
nzz.description: Der amerikanische Vizepräsident Vance ist am Sonntag in der Schweiz gelandet, um dort den Auftakt für die Verhandlungen mit Iran zu begleiten. Doch allein dieser erste Schritt gestaltete sich unerwartet schwierig.

nzz.title: Kieler Forscher: «Wir sollten Chinas Subventionen ausbeuten. Wenn uns China seine Produkte billig anbietet, sollten wir dieses Geschenk annehmen»
nzz.description: Der Konjunkturchef des Kieler Instituts für Weltwirtschaft, Stefan Kooths, warnt davor, Schutzzölle gegen Billigimporte aus China zu erheben. Sie belasteten die Konsumenten und bremsten den dringend nötigen Strukturwandel in Deutschland.

nzz.title: Sie hüten Kinder und pflegen Kultur: Eine Ehrenrettung der alten Schweizer
nzz.description: Senioren-Bashing ist gerade sehr beliebt. Zu Unrecht.

nzz.title: Präsident Karol Nawrocki hat Wolodimir Selenski den höchsten Orden Polens entzogen: Der Streit zwischen Polen und der Ukraine spitzt sich zu
nzz.description: Mehrere ukrainische Regierungsvertreter haben ebenfalls polnische Auszeichnungen abgelegt. Von der Beschädigung des Verhältnisses zwischen den beiden Verbündeten profitiert vor allem Moskau.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Neigen plötzlich alle Eidgenossen zur ökonomischen Selbstverstümmelung?
nzz.description: Die SVP ist zwar mit ihrer 10-Millionen-Initiative gescheitert, aber das Virus der Wachstumsmüdigkeit wütet nun in allen Lagern. Plötzlich steht die Standortförderung in der Kritik, das Freihandelsabkommen mit Mercosur vor dem Scheitern – und bald die Wettbewerbsfähigkeit auf dem Spiel.

nzz.title: Im Wallis soll ein Betreuer KI-Nacktbilder einer Schülerin erstellt haben – nun fordert der Nationalrat ein Verbot von Deepfakes
nzz.description: Der Aktionismus des Parlaments täuscht darüber hinweg, dass noch lange nichts passieren wird. Derweil explodiert die Masse an illegalem pornografischem Material im Internet, Ermittler stossen bereits jetzt an ihre Grenzen.

nzz.title: Leugnen, «trötzelen» oder sich kreativ rächen: Über die schwierige Kunst des Verlierens am Abstimmungssonntag
nzz.description: Auch in der Politik gilt: Gewinnen ist einfach, verlieren aber will gelernt sein, wie ein Blick in die jüngere Geschichte der Abstimmungen zeigt.

nzz.title: Umstrittenes Anlocken von Firmen: Im Zuge der Zuwanderungsdiskussion gerät nun die Standortpromotion des Bundes unter Druck
nzz.description: Politiker von links bis rechts stellen die Anwerbung von Firmen aus dem Ausland infrage. Der Bundesrat geht nun nochmals über die Bücher.

nzz.title: Ein Luxusresort für Jared Kushner, ein strategischer Baustein für Amerika: In Albanien zeigt sich, warum der Balkan plötzlich so wichtig ist für die USA
nzz.description: Auf der albanischen Insel Sazan planen Jared Kushner und Ivanka Trump ein Luxusresort. Gleichzeitig wollen die USA auf dem Balkan Gaspipelines und Kraftwerke bauen. Das ist kein Zufall.

nzz.title: Kurz vor Kriegsende: Iranischer Luftangriff zerstört Radarkuppel in Bahrain
nzz.description: Ein iranischer Angriff trifft den höchsten Punkt Bahrains, nur wenige Tage vor der Einigung zwischen den USA und Iran. Es könnte ein weiterer Schlag gegen die amerikanische Luftraumüberwachung am Golf sein.

nzz.title: Tadej Pogacar degradiert die Gegner an der Tour de Suisse zu Statisten – und bringt damit auch die Konkurrenz bei der Tour de France ins Grübeln
nzz.description: An der auf fünf Etappen verkürzten Tour de Suisse fährt der 27-jährige Slowene einem ungefährdeten Sieg entgegen. Zwei Wochen vor der Frankreich-Rundfahrt wirkt Pogacar unantastbar.

nzz.title: Jürgen Klopp und Thomas Müller sind als TV-Experten um keinen Scherz verlegen. Die Art und Weise ihrer Auftritte sagt viel über die beiden aus
nzz.description: Im Vorbeigehen zählt Jürgen Klopp den deutschen Nationaltrainer Julian Nagelsmann an. Dass dies absichtslos geschah, ist schwer zu glauben.

spiegel.title: Unwetter und Hitzerekorde: Wo es am Sonntag heftig wird
spiegel.description: Das Sommerwetter zeigt sich von seiner unangenehmen Seite: Neben extremer Hitze soll es auch zu starken Unwettern kommen. Besonders gefährlich sind überraschend auftretende Gewitter.

spiegel.title: WM 2026: Auf wen könnte Deutschland im Sechzehntelfinale treffen?
spiegel.description: Wie geht es nach dem Gruppensieg für die deutsche Fußballnationalmannschaft weiter? Und: Jubel um den Rekord-Torwart aus Curaçao, Trauer in Tunesien. Alles Wichtige im Blog.

spiegel.title: Russlands Angriffskrieg: Tote und Verletzte nach ukrainischen Drohnenangriffen auf der Krim
spiegel.description: Die Ukraine hat Ziele auf der von Russland annektierten Halbinsel Krim attackiert. Behördenangaben zufolge wurden mindestens vier Menschen getötet. In einem Kraftstoffterminal soll Feuer ausgebrochen sein.

spiegel.title: Rod Stewart wird bei Konzert in Utah fast ohnmächtig – dann spaßt er wieder
spiegel.description: Rod Stewart steht mit 81 Jahren noch auf der Bühne, bei einem Konzert in Utah allerdings auf etwas wackligen Beinen. Nach einer Sauerstofftank-Pause konnte er wieder mit dem Publikum lachen.

spiegel.title: Rentenkommission: DIW-Präsident Fratzscher kritisiert Pläne für Altersvorsorge
spiegel.description: Das Renteneintrittsalter soll maßvoll steigen, eine Kapitalrente das bisherige System ergänzen. Doch für den Topökonomen Marcel Fratzscher reicht dies nicht aus, die Schieflage des Systems zu beseitigen.

spiegel.title: Irankrieg: US-Vizepräsident JD Vance rechnet mit Fortschritten bei Iranverhandlungen
spiegel.description: Die Gespräche zwischen den USA und Iran sollen fortgesetzt werden. Vermittler und Vertreter der Kriegsparteien sind auf dem Weg in die Schweiz. JD Vance hofft auf Einigungen zu Teherans Atomfrage und der Waffenruhe im Libanon.

spiegel.title: News: Christliche Fußball-Spieler, WM 2026, SPIEGEL-Titel Krieg gegen Russland
spiegel.description: Wenn Nationalspieler im Stadion beten, wirkt das versöhnlich. Harmlos ist es nicht. Das ist die Lage am Sonntag.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM 2026: Deutschland siegt gegen die Elfenbeinküste - Kommentar: Die Geburt einer Mannschaft
spiegel.description: Das 2:1 im zweiten WM-Spiel kann das Bild der deutschen Nationalelf verändern: nach innen und nach außen. Dieser Sieg war wie ein Gründungsakt – dank Julian Nagelsmann.

spiegel.title: Hamburg: 14 Verletzte bei Brand in Hamburger Hotel
spiegel.description: Kurz nach Mitternacht musste die Feuerwehr zu einem Brand in einem Hotel in Hamburg ausrücken. Die Einsatzkräfte evakuierten die Menschen wegen starker Rauchbildung über Drehleitern.

spiegel.title: Edinburgh: Fünf Verletzte bei mutmaßlich muslimfeindlichen Angriffen
spiegel.description: Mit einer großen Waffe war ein 36-Jähriger durch Edinburgh gezogen und verletzte fünf Menschen. Laut Premierminister Keir Starmer soll der Mann aus Hass auf Muslime gehandelt haben. Schon bald soll er vor Gericht.

spiegel.title: Frankreich erlässt Alkoholverbot wegen Hitzewelle
spiegel.description: Am Sonntag werden in Frankreich Temperaturen von bis zu 40 Grad erwartet, ausgerechnet zur landesweiten Fête de la Musique. Um Rettungsdienste zu entlasten, gilt für den Tag ein großflächiges Alkoholverbot im öffentlichen Raum.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM 2026: Zweifacher Torschütze Deniz Undav wird nach Sieg über Elfenbeinküste gefeiert
spiegel.description: Publikumsliebling Deniz Undav hat mit seinen Toren Deutschland in die K.-o.-Phase geschossen – und das als Einwechselspieler. Der Frage, ob das so bleibt, kann der Bundestrainer jetzt nicht mehr ausweichen.

spiegel.title: 41-Jähriger in Krefeld nach Polizeischüssen gestorben
spiegel.description: Bei einem Einsatz im Stadtteil Uerdingen soll ein Mann zwei Polizisten mit einem Messer angegriffen haben. Ein Beamter verletzte den Verdächtigen schwer, er starb im Krankenhaus.

spiegel.title: Champigny-sur-Marne: Polizisten finden bei Drogenrazzia Picassogemälde
spiegel.description: Polizisten wollten in einem Haus in Champigny-sur-Marne Drogen sicherstellen. Bei der Razzia standen sie plötzlich vor einem waschechten Picasso. Die Ermittler gehen von Diebstahl aus.

spiegel.title: »The Death of Robin Hood«: Ein neuer Film zeigt unbekannte Facetten von Robin Hood
Sean Sherman: Essen wie bei Crazy Horse – indigene Küche ohne Kolonialzutaten
spiegel.description: »Sioux Chef« Sean Sherman betreibt ein erfolgreiches Restaurant, auf den Tisch kommen keine »kolonialen« Zutaten. Er sagt: Die indigene Küche ist auch besser für die Gesundheit.

new-sci.title: We've found a mysterious substance on Titan and Pluto
new-sci.description: Something is absorbing light on the surfaces of Pluto and Saturn’s moon Titan, and figuring out what it is could be crucial to understanding Titan’s complex chemistry

new-sci.title: Most portable air conditioners suck – but there's an easy fix
new-sci.description: Efficiency ratings on portable air conditioners don’t give consumers the full picture, and one type of aircon unit is so inefficient that it should be banned, says Michael Le Page

new-sci.title: Has the answer to life's origins been hiding in our cells all along?
new-sci.description: The surprising discovery of mysterious blobs inside our cells is revolutionising our understanding of how life works, and how it got started

new-sci.title: Gas from Uranus reveals it has an icy centre
new-sci.description: Carbon monoxide in Uranus's deep atmosphere indicates that the planet contains more ice than rock, suggesting it formed more like Neptune than we thought

new-sci.title: Can prebiotics, probiotics or postbiotics help your ageing microbiome?
new-sci.description: The disruption of your gut microbiome is a major consequence, and possible cause, of ageing. Columnist Graham Lawton looks into recent trials examining whether it can be replenished through diet and prebiotics, probiotics or postbiotics

new-sci.title: Remarkable fossils rewrite the story of how animals conquered the land
new-sci.description: Palaeontologists have found new evidence that the early ancestors of amphibians, reptiles and mammals did not have a larval stage with external gills like modern frogs or salamanders

new-sci.title: Almost the whole of Japan moved eastward after 2011 earthquake
new-sci.description: An extremely unusual tectonic movement took place 15 minutes after the Tohoku earthquake in 2011, causing almost the whole of Japan to move 5 millimetres to the east

new-sci.title: Carl Sagan's The Demon-Haunted World is still supremely relevant today
new-sci.description: Beautifully written, this guide to distinguishing between truth, misinformation and lies, first published in 1995, remains an essential read for anyone who considers themselves a critical thinker, says Leah Crane

new-sci.title: Complex life on Earth may last 500 million years longer than expected
new-sci.description: As the sun expands over the coming billions of years, Earth will become inhospitable to any life more complex than a microbe – but that might take longer than we thought

new-sci.title: New Scientist recommends an excellent look at the future of work
new-sci.description: Sarah O'Connor's We Are Not Machines explores how we are contorting ourselves to fit AI into our working lives – and what to do about it, finds Tom Knowles

new-sci.title: Ancient monument marked summer solstice centuries before Stonehenge
new-sci.description: Archaeologists have discovered traces of a wooden structure built 5000 years ago, 5 kilometres from Stonehenge, which appears to have been an even older monument for marking the summer solstice

new-sci.title: Cervical cancer deaths have plummeted thanks to HPV vaccine
new-sci.description: We already know the vaccine against human papillomavirus, or HPV, greatly reduces infections and cases of cervical cancer, and now we have the first evidence it prevents deaths too

new-sci.title: Chilling the body with drugs could limit brain damage from stroke
new-sci.description: Putting brain cells into a hibernation-like state via drugs that cool down core body temperature may help to preserve them following a stroke

new-sci.title: Oldest known plague outbreak killed hunter-gatherer children
new-sci.description: DNA evidence shows that plague bacteria devastated a community in Siberia more than 5000 years ago, challenging the idea that there were no major disease outbreaks before the advent of farming and large settlements

new-sci.title: Pigeons lock their eyes in place when they are flying
new-sci.description: Bird-mounted headsets and backpacks have revealed the surprising things pigeons do with their eyes when on the wing

phys-org.title: Climate change boosts soybean production but worsens bean quality
phys-org.description: A study published by Food Research International analyzed the triple effect of climate change on soybean quality—increased carbon dioxide (CO₂), high temperatures and drought. Using predictive modeling powered by artificial intelligence (AI) and based on experimentally verified data, the study assessed how these pressures would affect the beans. It concluded that the seeds would change their composition, producing 50% more beans but of lower nutritional quality.

phys-org.title: Bat rays employ a chemical cue to warn others of danger
phys-org.description: Frightened bat rays produce a chemical cue to warn other rays of danger, a well-known anti-predator strategy for bony fish that has not been documented in cartilaginous fish until now. Oregon State University researchers found the behavior of bat rays changed when they received water flow from a tank where another bat ray was frightened by a mock predator, suggesting that a chemical disturbance cue was passed from one tank to the other.

phys-org.title: Sonic booms from meteors can release the energy of hundreds of tons of TNT. Here's how they work
phys-org.description: As humans, we live out our lives on a planet that is constantly sweeping through a cosmic ocean littered with ancient debris from the formation of the solar system. For the most part, our world glides silently through space, shielded by Earth's thin atmosphere.

phys-org.title: Crane pair dances follow hidden rules, with performances revealing partner-driven timing
phys-org.description: Animal pairs engage in mutual signaling by simultaneously performing a diverse repertoire of behaviors. A famous example is the sophisticated dance (mutual displays) performed by bird pairs.

phys-org.title: Sunday is the longest day of the year for half the planet. A guide to the summer solstice
phys-org.description: This is the sun's time to shine: Sunday is the longest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere.

phys-org.title: Jumping gene caught moving between species in first direct observation
phys-org.description: Genes are not passed on exclusively from parents to their offspring. Some are mobile and can also jump to other species, as researchers at the Max Planck Institute for Marine Microbiology in Bremen have now shown. The direct observation of a jumping gene provides the first evidence that such genes can transfer from one species to another—from predator to prey. The study is published in the journal Scientific Reports.

phys-org.title: Ancient enamel just exposed a hidden human family entanglement that may still echo in your DNA
phys-org.description: An analysis of ancient teeth is giving scientists a rare peek into interactions between human relatives hundreds of thousands of years ago that have left a lasting imprint on our species.

phys-org.title: Radio scans find no alien tech from the latest interstellar comet
phys-org.description: The group leading the charge in the search for extraterrestrial life has given the all clear: An interstellar comet looks to be completely natural and free of any alien tech.

phys-org.title: Quantum gravity research links continuous parameters to local operators within the theory itself
phys-org.description: A researcher at Kyushu University and his collaborators have shown that continuous parameters in quantum gravity may not be freely adjustable "dials" from outside the theory, but rather arise from operators within the theory itself, supporting the century-old claim by Albert Einstein about the fundamental laws of nature.

phys-org.title: Eight ways to sleep well in hot weather
phys-org.description: When temperatures rise, sleep often suffers. Hot nights can make it harder to fall asleep, increase waking during the night and leave people feeling less rested the next day.

phys-org.title: New nanotube membranes reveal unusually fast lithium-ion transport
phys-org.description: Researchers have developed a novel class of nanotube membranes that enable ultrafast ion transport. The findings open new pathways for high-efficiency clean energy generation, lithium recovery and molecular separation.

phys-org.title: Herring weight and seal hunting markedly affecting the future of Baltic gray seals
phys-org.description: The carrying capacity of the Baltic Sea could withstand a seal population twice its current size, but hunting quotas and Baltic herring mean weight greatly affect the future of the seals. A recent study provides a new estimate for the carrying capacity of the Baltic gray seal population and accurate guidelines for decision-makers when determining hunting quotas.

phys-org.title: Ancient Mongolian cemetery reveals power and status mattered more than blood ties
phys-org.description: On the edge of the Mongolian steppe, overlooking where two rivers meet, lies an ancient cemetery. Buried within are two families, traced through ancient DNA across six generations, surrounded by dozens of "strangers." The obvious assumption is that this was a family cemetery. But a recent study used machine learning and a technique borrowed from evolutionary biology to reveal that what really mattered was wealth, status and political power, not blood.

phys-org.title: How much clothing is too much? The math behind having a sustainable wardrobe
phys-org.description: Most people suspect they own too many clothes, but they aren't sure exactly what the "right amount" is. Recent wardrobe studies, in which researchers literally peek inside people's closets, show the scale of the problem is far greater than most of us imagine.

phys-org.title: Faster aptamer screening finds synthetic alternatives to antibodies in days instead of months
phys-org.description: Aptamers are short DNA or RNA strands that can recognize and bind to a specific target molecule with high precision. Similar to antibodies, they can be used to detect these molecules or modulate their activity. Unlike antibodies, they are much more stable, can be produced synthetically and can be chemically modified to achieve the desired properties. As a result, they can offer capabilities that cannot be achieved with antibodies.

phys-org.title: Pumice rafts encroach on Admiralty Islands
phys-org.description: On May 8, 2026, satellites detected signs of an unexpected submarine volcanic eruption in the Bismarck Sea near the islands of Papua New Guinea. Over the next several weeks, plumes of steam and ash streamed over the sea, and areas of discolored water surrounded the eruption site. Relatively little is known about the ocean floor in this area or the volcanic feature that is presently erupting. But experts think the new activity, ongoing as of mid-June, might be occurring along the Titan Ridge and

phys-org.title: Antarctica is offering 30 to 50 years' worth of warning on sea level rise, models suggest
phys-org.description: Scientists predict that the next three to five decades provide a critical window to anticipate and plan for Antarctic ice loss and its contribution to sea level rise. Research published in Nature, led by Monash University researcher Dr. Felicity McCormack from Securing Antarctica's Environmental Future (SAEF), looks at the predictability of Antarctic ice loss and what this means for sea level rise projections.

phys-org.title: Australian farmers are desperate to escape the latest mouse plague—and may soon get relief
phys-org.description: For months, a flood of mice has engulfed Western Australia's agricultural regions. For people living through it, this latest mouse plague is all-consuming. Houses, sheds, paddocks and roads are blanketed with mice. And the smell of mice, both dead and alive, is impossible to escape.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

proj-syn.title: How (Not) to Conserve Tropical Forests
proj-syn.description: Although the Tropical Forest Forever Facility that emerged from the last United Nations Climate Conference is unlikely to succeed, critically important global conservation efforts are not doomed. proj-syn.title: Was Brexit Inevitable?
proj-syn.description: If counterfactual history is motivated by a refusal to accept what many have deemed inevitable, it is newly relevant now that the West is marking the tenth anniversary of the Brexit referendum. Even if Britain's fateful choice was caused by deeper structural and historical forces, that does not justify fatalism.

proj-syn.title: Questioning the Just War Doctrine
proj-syn.description: With war becoming more frequent and more lethal to civilians, Pope Leo XIV and the College of Cardinals are wading into the debate over its legitimacy. The best outcome of the “consistory” Leo is convening in in late June would be to authorize an overhaul of the just war doctrine for the modern era—and ask the necessary questions.

proj-syn.title: Bosnia Must Stand on Its Own
proj-syn.description: The Trump administration's recent, apparently corrupt intervention in Bosnia and Herzegovina could have been an opportunity finally to put the country on a path to full independence after more than 30 years of being a ward of the international community. Instead, the vicious cycle of dependence looks set to continue.

proj-syn.title: The Strategic Logic of the AI Arms Race
proj-syn.description: AI and drones are rapidly transforming warfare, shifting military power toward countries that can combine manufacturing scale, advanced AI systems, and battlefield data. The United States and Europe, hobbled by political dysfunction and obsolete military structures, remain dangerously unprepared.

proj-syn.title: The Meaning of Limited Government—Then and Now
proj-syn.description: In 1776, Adam Smith and America’s founders envisioned an economy that allowed individuals to pursue their own material well-being, with minimal government intervention. Today, America’s Republican Party claims to be committed to restoring that laissez-faire ideal, even as they make a mockery of its animating principles.

proj-syn.title: AI Sovereignty Is About Options, Not Ownership
proj-syn.description: The US government’s abrupt decision to suspend foreign access to Anthropic’s Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models clarifies what “AI sovereignty” is really about. In the emerging AI economy, competitive advantage will come not from owning a single model, but from being able to evaluate, select, and orchestrate many models.

proj-syn.title: The Promise and Peril of AGI
proj-syn.description: Artificial general intelligence could dramatically increase human prosperity and free people from countless mundane tasks. But unless its benefits and ownership are broadly shared, it could deprive billions of workers of their livelihoods and pave the way for a new form of techno-authoritarianism.

proj-syn.title: Reversing Brexit Is Labour’s Best Hope
proj-syn.description: When it comes to the relationship between the United Kingdom and the European Union, political expediency and economic logic both point in the same direction. A majority of British voters now believe that Brexit was a mistake, and they are looking for a leader who will put the issue back on the national agenda.

proj-syn.title: Global Health Reform Must Bolster Innovation
proj-syn.description: As funding falls for global public health, calls for a country-led system have grown louder. Such reforms are necessary, but they must not come at the expense of new vaccines, medicines, and diagnostics, which can be delivered by strengthening mechanisms—such as product development partnerships—that already work.

proj-syn.title: Learning from the Right Sovereign Wealth Funds
proj-syn.description: The Gulf has made establishing a sovereign wealth fund seem like a strategic—and glamorous—choice, leading countries like Canada to launch their own. But Latin America has run this experiment many times over the years, offering a more realistic view of an SWF’s pitfalls and promise.

proj-syn.title: Europe Cannot Afford Another Lost Year
proj-syn.description: European businesses need simpler rules, faster permitting, affordable energy, stronger infrastructure, and a fully functioning single market. The longer that European policymakers fail to deliver on these policies, the greater Europe’s competitiveness challenge will become.

proj-syn.title: White House Fight Night
proj-syn.description: The venue on the South Lawn for UFC Freedom 250 was built, approved, lit, filmed, defended, watched, and enjoyed as part of a celebration of freedom. President Donald Trump’s chosen object to represent that celebration was a cage.

proj-syn.title: The US-Iran Agreement Is a First Step
proj-syn.description: While the recently announced US-Iranian memorandum of understanding is certainly good news, it is not definitive. The path from a statement of diplomatic intent to a fully restored, non-inflationary energy supply chain is fraught with political, technical, and physical risks.

proj-syn.title: Developing-Country Risk Is Being Mispriced
proj-syn.description: When investors say there are no “bankable” projects in developing economies, they are typically referring less to project quality than to the cost of capital. But the assumptions driving up risk premia are not supported by the evidence, and until this changes, the misallocation of capital will continue to undermine development.

proj-syn.title: The Fed Has Been Honest and Stupid
proj-syn.description: It would be easy—and a mistake—to blame the US Federal Reserve’s many blunders on corrupt bureaucrats or imagined conspiracies. The truth of the matter is that the central bank relies on an outdated regional map and lagging indicators that no longer tell the whole story, while battling macroeconomic blazes that politicians stoke.

proj-syn.title: A New Framework for Climate Displacement
proj-syn.description: Global warming is already uprooting communities and impoverishing people who remain in vulnerable areas—a crisis that is often overshadowed by the focus on decarbonization. But the Global Climate Mobility Principles offer policymakers a framework for ensuring that these individuals maintain their agency and rights.

proj-syn.title: Peace With Iran Is All About Lebanon Now
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump says that he "calls the shots" on negotiating with Iran, and Israel has no choice but to submit to a deal that undermines its security interests. But a deal that makes Trump the protector of Lebanon—and, by extension, Iran-backed Hezbollah—could put the US and Israel on a collision course.

crunchbase.description: This week was not an exceptionally busy one for large funding deals, though we saw sizable rounds in a lively mix of sectors ranging from AI to fintech to quantum computing, biotech and cybersecurity.

crunchbase.title: AT&T Ventures’ Head Vikram Taneja On The New Rules of Seed-Stage Defensibility
crunchbase.description: In an interview with Crunchbase News, Vikram Taneja, head of AT&T Ventures, shares why he believes that while AI has drastically lowered the barrier to building software, it has also shifted the definition of seed-stage technical risk.

crunchbase.title: The Boardroom Blind Spot: When Success Hides Disruption
crunchbase.description: Boards should not wait for poor performance before confronting disruptive technologies like AI and quantum computing. Instead, writes guest columnist and strategic adviser Itay Sagie, they should evaluate the cost of inaction, challenge successful business models while they are still thriving, and proactively imagine how a technology-driven competitor could disrupt their company.

crunchbase.title: The Crunchbase Tech Layoffs Tracker
crunchbase.description: Over 127,000 workers at U.S.-based tech companies were laid off in mass job cuts in 2025, per a Crunchbase News tally, and the layoffs have continued into 2026. See the latest companies to cut roles.

crunchbase.title: ‘This System Wasn’t Built For Me’: Black Founders Became Investors To Change Venture Capital
crunchbase.description: The consistently low numbers of U.S. venture funding to Black founders led some to turn to investing in an effort to help level the playing field. Crunchbase News talked with two such founders to hear more about their experiences in raising capital and what they’ve learned from investing.

crunchbase.title: I Sold My AI Startup Before Revenue: Here’s What Investors Missed — And Founders Shouldn’t
crunchbase.description: The greatest long-term value in AI will come from companies solving deep technical challenges at the model and infrastructure level rather than application-layer products built on existing AI platforms, writes angel investor Alexander Kardos-Nyheim. In this guest commentary he shares processes and questions he uses to determine the investability of an AI startup.

crunchbase.title: SpaceX Acquires AI Coding Tool Cursor For $60B In Year’s Largest Startup M&A Deal
crunchbase.description: The acquisition of Cursor gives SpaceX a foothold into the enterprise software development market, where AI-assisted coding has taken off and led large companies to significantly pare back their reliance on human engineers.

crunchbase.title: Silicon Is Back: Playground Global’s Decade-Long Bet On Hardware, Energy And Deep Tech Looks Prescient
crunchbase.description: In the decade-plus since Playground Global's founding, it has built its investment thesis around the idea that breakthroughs in science and engineering — not just software — would create the next generation of valuable companies. Company co-founder Peter Barrett breaks it down in this Crunchbase News Q&A.

crunchbase.title: Rewriting Your Pitch: SaaS Isn’t Dead, But The Playbook For Founders Is Changing
crunchbase.description: Because AI and LLMs are reshaping the traditional SaaS model, founders are forced to focus less on software alone and more on delivering measurable business outcomes, defensible workflow ownership, strong retention, and efficient growth. Crunchbase guest author, Ivan Nikkhoo argues that rather than chasing trends like adding services, founders should build deep moats, understand customer workflows, adapt pricing toward usage- or outcome-based models, and prove that AI creates lasting value.

crunchbase.title: The AI Startup Funding Boom Is Not A Global Phenomenon
crunchbase.description: So far in 2026, U.S. companies have pulled in nearly 80% of global seed- through growth-stage financing, per Crunchbase data. That’s a sharp divergence from the years leading up to the AI boom, when American companies typically secured less than half of all investment.
